openQuestionsRoutedToOperator: The fix carries the glob into ONE workflow. Should it go into all three that produce `test`? The .gitattributes precedent added its path to all three because a checkout-policy change can break any of the three suites; a workflow-file change cannot break any of them, and this change only has to make the required context REPORT. All three would triple the CI cost of every workflow-only pull request and put three check-runs named `test` on heads that today produce one or two. This lane built the dispatch's smallest form; the wider form is the operator's ruling.

Should the required context set itself change? `test` is co-owned by three workflows and satisfied by any one of them succeeding, so a green `test` means 'one of three suites passed', not 'the suite passed'. Control D showed the duplicate-name condition is safe for the evaluation, but it also showed Command Center CI's `test` job skips its live-smoke step on every pull request while reporting `success`. A single always-on distinct-named context per suite is the structural fix; 91_branch_protection_runbook makes that a ruling with a reliability report behind it, and branch protection is not this lane's.

Should command-center-ci.yml's header comment be corrected? It prescribes the workaround (#415's measurement shows the workaround was never necessary) and this fix makes it more wrong: after #412, a command-center-ci.yml change also triggers Property Explorer CI. Reported, not edited.

Should the two 'should YES' root files (package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml) and the required-context's own checker (scripts/check-source-encoding.mjs) be added to a trigger? Each is a one-line path edit of the same shape as this fix, each can break or silently defang a suite a required check claims to protect, and each changes CI cost on ordinary pull requests — which is why this lane reports rather than builds them.
`packages/instrument-registry/**` ships `src/index.test.ts` that no workflow runs. Live package needing a producer, or dead code? Either answer is someone's decision.
